notes: «وَ شَكَا هِشَامُ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ إِلَى أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ» is the asker-then-asked form (rule 5): the Imam Ridha is the last link.
«قَالَ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ رَاشِدٍ وَ كُنْتُ دَائِمَ اَلْعِلَّةِ» continues a story inside the report, not a route; left out.
«وَ شَكَا هِشَامُ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ إِلَى أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ» is the asker-then-asked form (rule 5): the Imam Ridha is the last link.
«قَالَ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ رَاشِدٍ وَ كُنْتُ دَائِمَ اَلْعِلَّةِ» continues a story inside the report, not a route; left out.

«شكا هشام بن إبراهيم إلى أبي الحسن» opens the report: the complainant transmits the answer, then the one asked (rule 5; the Imam is the last link). Muhammad ibn Rashid's own account in the second half is not added as a link (scene in the story).
